A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboPEPP and contain complete main text and supplementary material. Corresponding equations, tables, plots and qualitative examples can be matched, including renumbered appendix figures.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendix report original robot pose, joint-angle, keypoint, occlusion, runtime and ablation results.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional learning-rate and architecture ablations in the appendix.

M1.justification: The pipeline and default architecture remain unchanged, including four Joint Net refinement steps and 256 Keypoint Net hidden channels. The expanded loss and gradient-scaling descriptions document implementation details without establishing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DREAM Panda, Kuka and Baxter sequences, synthetic occlusion tests and cluttered real-world qualitative examples. The added ablations reuse Panda data.

E2.justification: DREAM variants, HPE, HPE* and RoboPose retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. The new ablations vary RoboPEPP settings. RoboKeyGen remains discussed but is not directly evaluated.

E3.justification: New appendix experiments compare reversed or equalized Joint Net/Keypoint Net learning rates, refinement counts G=1–6, and hidden widths of 128, 256 and 512 channels. Previously reported splits, training budgets, metrics and default configurations are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices A2 and A5.3 add sensitivity analyses of fine-tuning learning-rate balance, Joint Net refinement depth and Keypoint Net capacity. These extend the retained pre-training, filtering, sim-to-real and occlusion ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional ablations continue to report point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables and plots retain their results; Table 4 only changes equivalent decimal formatting. New Table A3 reports AUCs of 69.3, 75.5 and 74.4 for 128, 256 and 512 channels. Appendix A2 adds Panda RS learning-rate controls scoring 71.9 and 76.4 alongside the retained 80.5 result, while Figure A3 adds refinement-count curves.

T1.justification: The kinematic assumptions and mathematical objectives are retained. Equation 3 spells out the previously named focal loss for implementation clarity; no new theoretical result, proof or mathematical reasoning is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning embedding predictive pre-training, pose and joint-angle accuracy, occlusion robustness and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.4 adds the hypothesis that DREAM's known-joint assumption lets it focus on keypoint detection. Appendix A2 interprets the learning-rate comparisons as evidence that robust keypoints guide Joint Net updates and explains gradient scaling as preventing conflicting encoder updates.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, explicit focal-loss exponents and normalization, a 1e-10 Keypoint Net learning rate, and 1e-10 scaling of gradients from its output. It also identifies Unreal Engine 4 as the synthetic-data source. Much of the architecture and training documentation was already present.

R1.justification: V2 adds Law and Deng's CornerNet reference alongside the focal-loss specification. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata and numbering; the related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording corrections, expands technical explanations, updates author affiliations and adds Appendix A5.3. The main section order and overall narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure A3 and Table A3, annotates Figure 4 with green peak-location arrows, and relocates Table A1. Qualitative figures are renumbered without changing their examples. On page 13, the new Figure A3 caption overlaps the A6 heading.

improvement.justification: V2 improves implementation clarity and reproducibility documentation, while targeted appendix ablations provide additional support for existing design choices. The main benchmark findings remain unchanged. These limited benefits outweigh the localized caption-heading overlap introduced on page 13.
